mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a mix of three modes of thought that are associated with Karl Marx, Husserl, and Heidegger."
Sartre's version of existentialism is a mix of three modes of thought that are associated with Karl Marx, Husserl, and Heidegger.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the fact that hermeneutics is a theory of interpretation. 1. __________ contribution to the history of modern hermeneutics distinguished it as a justification of the human sciences. 2."

Central to the entire discourse is the fact that hermeneutics is a theory of interpretation. 1. __________ contribution to the history of modern hermeneutics distinguished it as a justification of the human sciences. 2.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to the primary element in the being of a thing."
Essence refers to the primary element in the being of a thing.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a self- creating being who first exists, and then makes himself what he is because existence precedes essence."
Man is a self- creating being who first exists, and then makes himself what he is because existence precedes essence.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the strand of existentialism that tries to remove the idea of the transcendence from the existence of man in the world."
Atheistic existentialism is the strand of existentialism that tries to remove the idea of the transcendence from the existence of man in the world.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a social being and necessarily lives in the world."
Man by nature is a social being and necessarily lives in the world.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a dark realm of essences, as an intuitionism of a Bergsonian order, as an anti-scientific doctrine, or as a philosophy that denies the reality of the world by bracketing out existence" (1968:5)."

concern is a dark realm of essences, as an intuitionism of a Bergsonian order, as an anti-scientific doctrine, or as a philosophy that denies the reality of the world by bracketing out existence" (1968:5).
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the notion that human values are not created by anything external to man."
Implied in these Sartrean excerpts is the notion that human values are not created by anything external to man.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the most influential philosophical movement in contemporary Western philosophy."
Existentialism is the most influential philosophical movement in contemporary Western philosophy.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the man who has nothing to do with universal or societal moral codes."
The authentic man for Keirkegaard is the man who has nothing to do with universal or societal moral codes.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a theme that is common to all existentialists and it comes across as one of the characteristic features of human existence."
Anguish or its German equivalent-angst is a theme that is common to all existentialists and it comes across as one of the characteristic features of human existence.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a philosophical method often used to designate the method and movement that originated in the work of Edmund Husserl (1859 - 1938)."
Phenomenology is a philosophical method often used to designate the method and movement that originated in the work of Edmund Husserl (1859 - 1938).
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is considered a reaction to Hegel's attempt to bring the whole of reality, human beings inclusive, within his conceptual system."
Keikegaard's philosophy is considered a reaction to Hegel's attempt to bring the whole of reality, human beings inclusive, within his conceptual system.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the art of interpreting text which traditionally refers to the study of the interpretation of written texts in the areas of literature, religion and law."
Philosophical hermeneutics is the art of interpreting text which traditionally refers to the study of the interpretation of written texts in the areas of literature, religion and law.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to this as the act of intentionality which is the defining characteristic of consciousness."
Husserl refers to this as the act of intentionality which is the defining characteristic of consciousness.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the unique source of value and there is no God to determine human value - the movement from the realm of 'in-itself' to 'for-itself'."
Man's freedom is the unique source of value and there is no God to determine human value - the movement from the realm of 'in-itself' to 'for-itself'.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the reason that man is faced with the absurdities in the world."
Man's alienation from the infinite-God is the reason that man is faced with the absurdities in the world.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to the German tradition of self-cultivation; it implies creation, image or shape."
Bildung refers to the German tradition of self-cultivation; it implies creation, image or shape.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an existential phenomenon according to Heidegger."
Death is an existential phenomenon according to Heidegger.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is considered to be fundamentally free ontologically as his very existence implies his freedom."
The human person is considered to be fundamentally free ontologically as his very existence implies his freedom.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the mode in which you find other beings, while man as a conscious subject exists as being-for-itself."
Being-in-itself is the mode in which you find other beings, while man as a conscious subject exists as being-for-itself.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the realm of human freedom and consciousness."
Being-for-itself is the realm of human freedom and consciousness.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a German word that is very fundamental to Heidegger's existentialist philosophy."
Dasein is a German word that is very fundamental to Heidegger's existentialist philosophy.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the idea of a rigorous science and this is why Husserl emphasises the eidetic science; the science aimed at discovering the essence of things."
The constant feature of Husserlian phenomenology is the idea of a rigorous science and this is why Husserl emphasises the eidetic science; the science aimed at discovering the essence of things.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the fact that anything happening now had happened in the past and will happen again in the future."
Implied in this doctrine is the fact that anything happening now had happened in the past and will happen again in the future.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a form of determinism (See Omoregbe 1991:97)."
Belief in human nature is a form of determinism (See Omoregbe 1991:97).
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a way of describing rather than a way of explaining."
The phenomenological method is a way of describing rather than a way of explaining.
fib: ______ is the Latinised version of the Greek word hermeneutice which has been part of the everyday language since the 17th century.
Hermeneutics
Hermeneutics is the Latinised version of the Greek word hermeneutice which has been part of the everyday language since the 17th century.
______ refers to how the meaning of the discourse depends on the general structure of the language it uses; therefore, it is a matter of general linguistic structures.
grammatical side
The grammatical side refers to how the meaning of the discourse depends on the general structure of the language it uses; therefore, it is a matter of general linguistic structures.
______ refers to the that which is in being.
Existence
Existence refers to the that which is in being.
______ is the ideal man who embodies the master morality.
'superman
The 'superman' is the ideal man who embodies the master morality.
______ is the inevitability of choice since to be free is to be compelled to choose.
Along with freedom too
Along with freedom too is the inevitability of choice since to be free is to be compelled to choose.
______ are the notions of 'existence precedes essence' and 'human freedom.' Sartre is an atheistic existentialist.
Central to Sartre's existentialist thoughts
Central to Sartre's existentialist thoughts are the notions of 'existence precedes essence' and 'human freedom.' Sartre is an atheistic existentialist.
______ is a whole, focused, single individual.
'I' of the I-Thou relationship
The 'I' of the I-Thou relationship is a whole, focused, single individual.
______ refers to his past, fallenness refers to his present, and existentiality refers to his future.
Facticity
Facticity refers to his past, fallenness refers to his present, and existentiality refers to his future.
______ is a method of bracketing of our presuppositions in our understanding of objects.
Epoche
Epoche is a method of bracketing of our presuppositions in our understanding of objects.
______ means to abstain from asserting phenomena as real or appearance.
Husserlian bracketing simply
Husserlian bracketing simply means to abstain from asserting phenomena as real or appearance.
______ is the directedness towards a transcendental object.
Intentionality
Intentionality is the directedness towards a transcendental object.
______ is the capacity for negation and nihilation, which characterises the being-for-itself.
Freedom for him
Freedom for him is the capacity for negation and nihilation, which characterises the being-for-itself.
______ is the recognition of a possibility as our possibility.
Anguish
Anguish is the recognition of a possibility as our possibility.
______ refers to Gadamer's hermeneutics as politically naïve.
Habermas
Habermas refers to Gadamer's hermeneutics as politically naïve.
______ is a type of existentialism which posits that human existence is meaningful insofar as it involves personal relationship with God.
Theistic existentialism
Theistic existentialism is a type of existentialism which posits that human existence is meaningful insofar as it involves personal relationship with God.
______ refers to here is the tendency to view philosophy through the mirror of the natural sciences because of the successes that the natural sciences have recorded.
chaotic situation Husserl
The chaotic situation Husserl refers to here is the tendency to view philosophy through the mirror of the natural sciences because of the successes that the natural sciences have recorded.
______ is a process by which the subject reduces his natural self as well as his psychological life to the transcendental and phenomenological experience.
Transcendental reduction
Transcendental reduction is a process by which the subject reduces his natural self as well as his psychological life to the transcendental and phenomenological experience.
______ is described as non-substantial and contentless, that is, as "entirely activity and spontaneity," "self-determining," "self-activated" and, therefore, free (Sartre;1956:iv).
Consciousness
Consciousness is described as non-substantial and contentless, that is, as "entirely activity and spontaneity," "self-determining," "self-activated" and, therefore, free (Sartre;1956:iv).
______ is the concrete actualisation of freedom.
Choice
Choice is the concrete actualisation of freedom.
______ is a possibility to become what he is not yet.
Man as being
Man as being is a possibility to become what he is not yet.
______ is the stage through which we change all that is given in experience into a phenomenon.
phenomenal reduction
The phenomenal reduction is the stage through which we change all that is given in experience into a phenomenon.
______ is the view that we experience meaning when we bracket lived experience.
Reduction
Reduction is the view that we experience meaning when we bracket lived experience.
______ is the father of existentialism - he articulated the basic themes of existentialism.
Kierkegaard
Kierkegaard is the father of existentialism - he articulated the basic themes of existentialism.
______ is the life lived by the free choice of the individual.
authentic life
The authentic life is the life lived by the free choice of the individual.
______ refers to the individual's possibility of choice (Maclntyre :149).
Freedom
Freedom refers to the individual's possibility of choice (Maclntyre :149).
______ is used by existentialists, especially Heidegger, to describe a state of living with a highly meaningful orientation aimed at achieving personal growth.
being-in-the-world
A being-in-the-world is used by existentialists, especially Heidegger, to describe a state of living with a highly meaningful orientation aimed at achieving personal growth.
